page: Microsoft Azure D16ds_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Ddsv6 family, operating under Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is equipped with an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at up to 4.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading (2 threads per core). Memory capacity is configured at 64 GB, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 4 GB per virtual core. High-speed local temporary storage is bundled via an integrated 945 GB NVMe SSD. The processor features 260 MB of L3 cache and supports instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel AMX matrix extensions. No discrete GPU accelerators are present.

Benchmark results position the D16ds_v6 predominantly in the middle tier of general compute and memory performance. The instance achieved a PassMark CPU score of 22,224.0 and Geekbench scores of 1,778.0 for single-core and 10,435.0 for multi-core. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reached 105.59 GB/sec alongside 54.61 GB/sec write throughput. The platform demonstrates top-quartile performance in select text and inference metrics, including a Geekbench text processing score of 2,519.0 and small-model (135M parameter) LLM generation throughput of 292.48 tokens per second. In data service benchmarks, it produced 19.51 million Redis SET operations per second and 24.09 GB/sec static web serving throughput.

The qualitative cost profile of the instance benefits from the bundled 945 GB NVMe SSD, which eliminates the need for external network storage for workloads dependent on fast scratch volumes or caching tiers. With its balanced processor and memory ratio, the D16ds_v6 is suited for multi-tier web applications, relational and key-value databases, continuous integration build agents, and search or text processing pipelines. Applications requiring specialized GPU compute or higher RAM density per core require different platform families.
description: The Microsoft Azure D16ds_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor delivering clock speeds up to 4.2 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture, it provides 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores, paired with 64 GB of memory adhering to a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Local ephemeral storage is supplied via a bundled 945 GB NVMe SSD. The CPU incorporates 260 MB of L3 cache along with AVX-512 and AMX vector extensions, without discrete GPU hardware. Synthetic testing demonstrates consistent mid-range compute performance, achieving a PassMark CPU score of 22,224.0 and Geekbench scores of 1,778.0 single-core and 10,435.0 multi-core, with upper-quartile results in text processing and small-model inference. Supporting over 19 million Redis SET operations per second and 24.09 GB/sec static web throughput, the D16ds_v6 is designed for web serving, microservices, databases, and CI/CD pipelines needing high-speed local scratch disk.
